head: 747184313c08b48c601f66be7d63bad04d7703b0
scope: Read-only native reconciliation; report/doc edits only; no new build or device installation

comments.title: First launch / onboarding order
comments.request: The app needs to welcome the user first, then ask for their level of knowledge in poker. Right now it is the opposite way. Can we do this first?
comments.current: Welcome → optional starting check → first lesson is wired in RootView. The unchanged comparison content is a separate issue.
comments.required: Recheck a fresh Release launch with no demo hooks; observe the screen on the phone.

comments.title: Start guide / hand comparison variety
comments.request: The comparisons are A pair vs K pair, then 10 pair vs 8 pair. Add 3–5 more varied comparisons, including three of a kind, straights and flushes.
comments.current: Only two pair comparisons are on the default path. Trips, straight and flush are behind an optional wrap-up button.
comments.required: Make varied hand types part of the main intro, explain each type before its comparison, and update progress and back navigation. Test the default path without tapping extra practice.

comments.title: First lesson / incorrect-answer feedback alignment
comments.request: Deliberately chose a wrong answer. The My answer Tie → Correct Opponent wins spacing and alignment is inconsistent.
comments.current: VerdictRow now separates labels from values; correct responses have one confirmation.
comments.required: Retain this structure; verify long dynamic values, wrong/near/right and restored states.

comments.title: App-wide narrator voice / answer choices versus feedback
comments.request: Correct I win should be Correct you win. Choices naturally use the user perspective (my hand/opponent hand); feedback should speak from the app to the user (yes, you won). Audit this throughout the app.
comments.current: Shared feedback uses app-addressed outcome wording. The broader copy audit is not complete: restored views retain raw terminology and equity-as-win-chance wording.
comments.required: Finish a context-sensitive scan of live, restored, archived and spoken strings. Choices may use user perspective; feedback must use one normalized outcome.

comments.title: Count the pot / blind explanation and cumulative worked guide
comments.request: Include a brief small-blind/big-blind explanation in the lesson. Keep each equation visible and append the next below it instead of replacing screens on Next. Build gradually with smooth animation, then ask the final number and let the user check.
comments.current: Pot walkthrough explains blinds, retains earlier contribution rows and keeps the final total covered for a tap answer.
comments.required: Retain cumulative reasoning. Exercise Previous, answer/reveal, interruption and reduced motion.

comments.title: Count the pot / replay controls and hint presentation
comments.request: Previous action and Next action buttons are cut off. Hint opens a full-screen sheet with little content and wastes space; explore options, perhaps center-aligned.
comments.current: Bottom safe-area layout and explicit replay controls replace the overlapping layout; short guidance is compact and reopenable.
comments.required: Verify scroll-and-tap reachability, not just an initial screenshot, at mini normal/AX5 sizes.

comments.title: Who acts first / beginner acronyms and teaching-area layout
comments.request: In new beginner mode, lesson3 shows Order before the flop and a UTG → UTG+1 → LJ → HJ → CO... chain in the bottom bar. The acronyms are unknown and the middle is mostly empty. Put important lesson information in the middle; reserve the bottom for Next or choices. Change this.
comments.current: Live position teaching uses numbered boxes and meaningful labels. Restored committed answers still show the old acronym strip.
comments.required: Use the same beginner position component and plain names after relaunch. Remove the restored position text-size cap.

comments.title: Navigation model / edge-swipe back and revisiting lesson steps
comments.request: Current navigation mostly uses arrow controls and screens sliding up from the bottom. Incorporate the familiar left-edge swipe right to go back, either mixed with bottom-up components or replacing the navigation approach. Current lessons, especially the beginning guide, also need an option to go back.
comments.current: Previous/edge-back exists in first guide, walkthrough, basic guide, node/practice/review and Free Table; a uniform app-wide navigation audit is not complete.
comments.required: List every hierarchy/help wrapper and verify edge-back, visible Back and Close destinations. Preserve committed answers and distinguish revisiting a step from pausing the activity.

comments.title: Lesson info/help / example completion and conflicting Back/Close
comments.request: Who acts first info → Watch an example → I understand at the end appears to do nothing. Top-left back arrow and top-right down arrow are confusing. Audit every lesson and help button; consider edge back.
comments.current: Example completion now has Check example before Finish, with distinct return-to-explanation and close-to-question callbacks.
comments.required: The reported original no-response was not reproduced. Current representative route checks do not prove every help wrapper; include each in the next interaction pass.

comments.title: Who acts first / full beginner lesson overhaul
comments.request: Early/Middle/Late/Blinds seating chart is not understandable for a new user. Explain each position and the flow through an eight-person table before asking questions; use the empty middle better.
comments.current: Eight-seat box-loop teaching demonstrates roles and pre/postflop order, but the restored position path bypasses it.
comments.required: Complete the same overhaul in resumed reveals and verify the teaching-before-question route for a new learner.

comments.title: Should I enter first / first-use notation and app-wide terminology
comments.request: The guide shows king of spades and six of spades then immediately K6s, which a beginner will not understand. Explain every poker term before using it and ease users into poker language.
comments.current: RFI introduces physical cards and suit notation, but open/direct practice and references can still use unexplained shorthand such as 3벳.
comments.required: Provide short contextual definitions wherever first entry is possible, including direct practice, graded chart and restored screens.

comments.title: Should I enter first / hand-score cognitive load
comments.request: Calculating hand score is too difficult right now. Treat the learner as a beginner.
comments.current: Beginner Chen score arithmetic is optional detail rather than a prerequisite.
comments.required: Retain the simpler decision path; test whether beginners can proceed without opening score math.

comments.title: First hand chart / axes, cells, notation and legend onboarding
comments.request: Before the first hand-strength chart, explain what it is, how to read it, each axis, each cell, and broad orientation such as top-left strong hands and high cards near the top.
comments.current: A shared chart primer explains axes, pairs, suited/offsuit cells and color. Direct Defend questions omit it; graded chart reading help starts collapsed.
comments.required: Teach chart reading before first meaningful use on every entry route. Explain high ranks near the top/left; avoid implying that every top-left cell is universally best or chart color means win chance.

comments.title: Lesson hint footprint / persistent lightbulb panel
comments.request: The lightbulb section at the top of lessons takes up too much space. Consider a nice small popup that disappears after 2–3 seconds.
comments.current: The large cue became a compact disclosure that remains available.
comments.required: The approved refinement keeps guidance reopenable rather than removing essential instructions after 2–3 seconds.

comments.title: Answer feedback / distinct app-voiced labels and layout
comments.request: Again My answer Raise → Correct Fold should use Your answer. Prefer clearer separation: Your answer: Raise → Correct answer: Fold.
comments.current: Your answer / Correct answer are distinct label-value rows. Correct semantic outcomes collapse to one confirmation.
comments.required: Keep this across live and restored results, including VoiceOver labels.

comments.title: Defend header spacing
comments.request: Hint and Try together are too close; screenshot shows cramped header spacing.
comments.current: The Defend header uses shared compact cue/chrome rather than the crowded old lightbulb panel.
comments.required: Retain; check both languages and themes on compact and AX layouts.

comments.title: Chart-supported beginner practice
comments.request: Show the chart while answering first, then offer answering without it after multiple correct answers; current difficulty is too high.
comments.current: Beginner Defend provides visible chart support and hide/reopen controls. There is no progress-triggered invitation to try without the chart.
comments.required: Keep chart use voluntary with no public helped/solo distinction. Add a gentle optional invitation after repeated correct decisions if retaining that original progression idea; never force help off.

comments.title: Defend question variety
comments.request: Most answers in the completed section were Fold; mix strong and weak hands.
comments.current: New scheduled Defend lessons select a seed covering Fold, Call and Re-raise across the three graded questions.
comments.required: This balances scheduled lesson questions, not every arbitrary practice round. Verify repeats and immutable saved-session seeds.

comments.title: Beginner curriculum order
comments.request: Move Which cards turn it around earlier; learn winning hands and playing before percentages and math, which may disengage beginners.
comments.current: Curriculum puts showdown and turn-changing cards before pot counting and percentage topics.
comments.required: Verify the real fresh-user recommendation sequence, including basics, rather than relying on a reordered lesson list alone.

comments.title: One-tap answer input across lessons
comments.request: Use two or three choices instead of manual numeric input in Which cards turn it around and all lessons; minimize touches.
comments.current: Beginner count, estimate and range routes use two/three tap choices. Advanced calibration retains optional numeric/interval entry.
comments.required: Treat advanced calibration as an intentional exception; ensure no beginner route unexpectedly opens manual entry.

comments.title: Grouped river-card outcomes / easier comparison
comments.request: User discovered that tapping a card already shows both final hands, so the missing-explanation concern is partly withdrawn. Improve organization by grouping equivalent card outcomes rather than requiring redundant taps through the same rank in different suits.
comments.current: Live outs groups use both players’ best-five rank signatures and winner. Restored outs still expose individual card lists.
comments.required: Carry the organized group comparison into restored/review states while preserving meaningful suit/kicker differences.

comments.title: Variation on repeated guides and lessons
comments.request: Provide different hands and questions each time a user repeats any guide or lesson; consider a bigger stored question bank.
comments.current: Rotating seeds improve generated lessons, but first-guide variety is mostly suit/player swaps and three fixed extra boards. Basics and learning-guide checks remain fixed.
comments.required: Build a semantically varied curated/generative bank for every repeatable quiz guide and lesson. Avoid immediate repeats; keep saved seeds stable. Verify different concepts/outcomes, not just suit changes.

comments.title: Free Play / help navigation labels
comments.request: Hint, This Hand and Rules have unclear meaning; user cannot predict what each page shows. Improve phrasing and wording.
comments.current: Free Play destinations say Decision help, Hand history and Table guide.
comments.required: Confirm labels predict their content at four/eight players and in screen-reader navigation.

comments.title: Localized table player names / consistent seat layout
comments.request: Use short English names in English games and Korean-spelled English names in Korean tables. Prefer consistent three-character Korean names and short English names to avoid name-related spacing/alignment problems. Examples: 토마스, 마이클, 알렉스, 클로이, 소라, 세라, 데이비드.
comments.current: Names are centralized and localized to short English names and Korean transliterations.
comments.required: Verify the actual longest name across supported seat counts; equal characters alone do not guarantee equal width.

comments.title: Quick Play / ten-hand session recap and complete hand review
comments.request: After Quick Play (10 hands), show an overall casual recap and let the user go through all hands. Pair one general phrase with exact numbers, such as frequent calls/raises, chart matches, risks versus safe play, successful bluffs or luck. Serve casual and mathematically interested users.
comments.current: Quick Game recap has a factual most-frequent-action sentence, exact denominators and per-hand archive review.
comments.required: Run an actual ten-hand session through recap, all ten reviews, cold restart and retention. No invented bluff intent, luck or universal optimality claims.

comments.title: Free Play / mid-game exit and new-game navigation
comments.request: Need a button to quit during a game. Returning shows only Continue the free table and prevents starting another game; Change the Table appears only after finishing the hand. Explore clearer wording such as Start new game.
comments.current: End game and Start new game are available mid-hand; close pauses, confirmed replacement discards unfinished play while retaining settled records.
comments.required: Retain confirmations and atomic persistence; recheck save-failure/resume paths when touched.

comments.title: Progress and app-wide information hierarchy / text density
comments.request: Progress is fine overall but has too much text and no diagrams or graphics, making it overwhelming. Add clearer sections/categories so the app feels less like a collection of text blocks.
comments.current: Progress leads with actual completion, seven-day markers, recent topics and track bars; detailed metrics are collapsed.
comments.required: Retain meaningful graphics. Check empty/sparse/full history and whether the resulting page feels understandable to a beginner.

comments.title: Settings / compact preferences, sound and haptics
comments.request: Language and appearance controls are too large. Make them compact and move them lower because they rarely change. Research other apps Settings flow, add separate sound on/off and haptic on/off settings, and investigate the menu more deeply.
comments.current: Compact lower-page language/appearance menus and separate persistent sound/haptic switches exist; actual feedback reads preferences.
comments.required: Document intended feedback events and verify off/on behavior on device. Toggle existence alone does not prove audible/tactile coverage.

gaps.title: Make the main intro actually varied
gaps.acceptance: Current: pair → pair → action explanation → wrap-up; extra hand types are optional. Required: progressive required comparisons with trips, straight and flush, each explained in plain language; preserve a visible skip and Previous.

gaps.title: Finish first-use chart and vocabulary teaching
gaps.acceptance: Current: useful teaching exists in a walkthrough or disclosure. Required: first-time direct practice and graded-mode entry also teach how to read the chart and define 3-bet, bb, call/raise before expecting the learner to use them.

gaps.title: Give repeated guides genuinely different questions
gaps.acceptance: Current: shuffled fixed boards/suits, a fixed basics check and fixed learning-guide checks. Required: distinct hand structures, strengths and outcomes with a bounded repeat-avoidance policy. Rotation must never mutate an active saved question.

gaps.title: Bring restored screens up to the new design
gaps.acceptance: Current: resumed position answers retain raw acronyms and capped text; restored ranges lose guessed outline and missing/extra lists; restored outs use the older individual-card layout. Required: reuse current teaching/evidence components after relaunch without changing grades or stored bytes.

gaps.title: Correct equity wording on primary and restored paths
gaps.acceptance: Current: the equity question says “How often do you win?”; Korean walkthrough equates win count with equity, while grading includes shares of ties. Required: explain equity as wins plus the user’s share of ties in both languages; keep grading unchanged.

gaps.title: Complete navigation and help-route consistency
gaps.acceptance: Current: many screens have edge-back and Previous, but no complete route-by-route acceptance evidence. Required: explicit Back/Close destinations, safe gestures, working finish controls and unchanged saved answers on every help wrapper.

gaps.title: Close the beginner guided-game bridge
gaps.acceptance: Current: ordered concepts and separate Free/Graded Play exist, but the accepted compare → pot → call/check → guided hand → independent review path is not established as one complete beginner route. Required: make the continuation understandable and verify its end-to-end path.

gaps.title: Sign off layout parity and actual device behavior
gaps.acceptance: Current: 140 historical build-18 fixture frames and targeted interaction passes, not every screen/state. Required: route matrix EN/KO × light/dark, mini normal/AX5, long values, restore, errors and scrolling; matched meaningful normal wrapping, natural Korean, native accessibility and physical feedback checks.

earlyDecisions.D02: Partial: fraction presentation exists; primary and restored equity wording needs G05.
earlyDecisions.D03: Partial: shared/missing/extra evidence exists live but is absent on restored range answers (G04).
earlyDecisions.D04: Partial: welcome-first is wired; broader varied default intro needs G01.
earlyDecisions.D05: Implemented in source: comparison teaching and optional rank/occurrence facts are distinct; novice comprehension remains unverified.
earlyDecisions.D06: Implemented in source: compact contextual cue and reserved bottom space; all-state occlusion verification remains G08.
earlyDecisions.D07: Implemented: completion/recent-topic Progress with expandable detail.
earlyDecisions.D08: Implemented: completion-first summaries; public helped/solo split superseded.
earlyDecisions.D09: Implemented: completed Free Play help offers review/next-hand actions.
earlyDecisions.D10: Partial: everyday live titles exist; restored jargon/labels need G04.
earlyDecisions.D11: Implemented live: blinds/button and pre/postflop action order; restored position needs G04.
earlyDecisions.D12: Implemented in source: aligned level semantics and explanation of effects.
earlyDecisions.D13: Implemented in source: Free and Graded Play have distinct purposes.
earlyDecisions.D14: Implemented: preflop chart-relative and postflop simplified-model feedback; beginner unit definitions need G02.
earlyDecisions.D15: Implemented: two physical AA combinations precede AA/six-combo explanation.
earlyDecisions.D16: Partial: one coherent guided-game-to-independent-review path needs G07.
earlyDecisions.D17: Validation pending: targeted controls passed earlier; not every route/state is signed off.
earlyDecisions.D18: Validation pending: four normal language/theme states plus AX behavior across every touched live/restored path.
earlyDecisions.D19: Preserved: felt/card identity, amber navigation/selection and equal uncommitted options.
earlyDecisions.D20: Report rule: historical capture, native fixture, proposal and unverified outcome must remain distinct.

perspectives.title: Put the topic above the count
perspectives.recommendation: Lead with “Practised: Compare hands”; put “3 questions completed” beneath it.
perspectives.status: Implemented: lesson topic precedes question count.

perspectives.title: Records should help someone return
perspectives.recommendation: Add a compact recent-topic row and a meaningful next action.
perspectives.status: Implemented: recent topics and continuation are in Progress.

perspectives.title: Align typography with inset roles
perspectives.recommendation: Use a shared semantic role and measure visible script ink in native KO and EN.
perspectives.status: Validation pending: full native inset/ink alignment is not signed off.

perspectives.title: Meaning outranks exact line parity
perspectives.recommendation: Prefer concise equivalent translations; allow natural AX reflow without shrinking type.
perspectives.status: Validation pending: normal-language wrapping and natural AX reflow.

perspectives.title: An example before EV and ranges
perspectives.recommendation: Show one concrete hand and a plain-language reason before introducing shorthand.
perspectives.status: Partial: chart/EV first-use routes need the concrete-example audit (G02).

perspectives.title: Keep equal choices and the commit boundary
perspectives.recommendation: Preserve equally weighted answers, learner freedom, and explanations after commitment.
perspectives.status: Preserved invariant: equal choices and no uncommitted answer reveal.

perspectives.title: A signature teaching interaction
perspectives.recommendation: Extend the existing worked guide and replay: after commitment, offer a visible “Compare five cards” action that identifies each best five-card hand.
perspectives.status: Partial: live best-five comparison exists; complete resumed comparison consistency.

perspectives.title: Inclusivity needs native proof
perspectives.recommendation: Verify VoiceOver reading order, spoken card labels, Dynamic Type, contrast and reachable controls on the native app.
perspectives.status: Validation pending: physical VoiceOver and complete native accessibility.

perspectives.title: Quiet delight can be useful
perspectives.recommendation: Make a correct explanation and a calm next step the satisfying moment; check reduced motion on a device.
perspectives.status: Validation pending: reduced-motion and physical feedback feel.

perspectives.title: Do not manufacture innovation or impact
perspectives.recommendation: Describe supported qualities plainly; leave innovation and social-impact claims unmade.
perspectives.status: Preserve: no invented innovation or impact claims.

perspectives.title: A credible module boundary
perspectives.recommendation: Show one invariant with the relevant source and test instead of a long feature inventory.
perspectives.status: Documentation/evidence: package separation exists; keep a concise invariant case study.

perspectives.title: Explain exact versus sampled equity
perspectives.recommendation: Explain when exact enumeration or seeded Monte Carlo is used, and how fixtures guard correctness.
perspectives.status: Partial: method disclosures exist, but equity/tie wording needs G05.

perspectives.title: Recovery behavior is a strong case study
perspectives.recommendation: Demonstrate a failed load, preserved backup and successful recovery without rewriting history.
perspectives.status: Existing recovery behavior and prior tests; demonstrate a current recovery case before portfolio claims.

perspectives.title: Close one native learner loop
perspectives.recommendation: Deliver and verify one end-to-end native path: start, decide, reveal, finish, reopen and resume.
perspectives.status: Partial: an end-to-end beginner route with return/resume needs explicit acceptance.

perspectives.title: Show who made which decision
perspectives.recommendation: Explain one decision personally made, one failure fixed and one tested tradeoff. Map AI or agent assistance to design, implementation and review ownership.
perspectives.status: Portfolio work: transparent personal decisions, failures, tradeoffs and AI contribution narrative still needs a final artifact.

perspectives.title: Public simplification preserves private truth
perspectives.recommendation: Keep factual committed-answer feedback and recovery history when simplifying the public summary.
perspectives.status: Preserved: public simplification retains internal grades/help metadata and recovery.

perspectives.title: Make fit visible in one glance
perspectives.recommendation: Lead with what it is, whom it serves, your verified contribution and current status.
perspectives.status: Portfolio work: role/contribution/current-status presentation is separate from app shipping.

perspectives.title: A real walkthrough beats a report tour
perspectives.recommendation: Record one decision, the reason revealed, and a return to saved progress after native verification.
perspectives.status: Not evidenced: a real 60–90 second project walkthrough recording.

perspectives.title: Repair reviewer-facing documentation drift
perspectives.recommendation: Check the current implementation and refresh README course/default descriptions with an implemented-versus-proposed legend.
perspectives.status: Implemented in README: tracks/defaults and current progress semantics updated.

perspectives.title: Tailor the evidence to the role
perspectives.recommendation: For iOS show SwiftUI, recovery and accessibility; for UX show the research gap and decision process; for algorithms show invariants and fixtures.
perspectives.status: Portfolio work: tailor evidence to the target role, not a new app feature.

perspectives.title: Start with one achievable idea
perspectives.recommendation: Preserve the current narrow card decision and validate transfer with an unseen example before broadening.
perspectives.status: Partial: narrow pair transfer exists; new varied intro still needs G01 and actual novice transfer validation.

perspectives.title: Whose cards, whose turn?
perspectives.recommendation: Label my cards, the other hand and shared cards; explain the five-card selection after a committed answer.
perspectives.status: Implemented live: ownership and best-five explanation; restore parity needs G04.

perspectives.title: Returning should not feel like punishment
perspectives.recommendation: State what the dates mean and keep gaps neutral. Test reopening an interrupted lesson after a gap.
perspectives.status: Implemented copy/data: neutral date gaps; real return-after-gap testing remains.

perspectives.title: Keep help free of judgment
perspectives.recommendation: Keep the visible help choice and an honest correction with one next step.
perspectives.status: Preserved: freely available help and honest correction without public help categories.

perspectives.title: Betting language needs concrete amounts
perspectives.recommendation: Show a worked chip example before shorthand and disclose assumptions when explaining a grade.
perspectives.status: Partial: concrete chips exist; direct bb/3-bet definitions remain G02.

perspectives.title: Listen to actual no-poker beginners
perspectives.recommendation: Run an exploratory study with 5–8 participants, split between KO and EN, who have no poker experience.
perspectives.status: Not performed/evidenced: 5–8 no-poker participants across Korean/English. This cannot be replaced with synthetic fixtures.
